abstract: Many unconditional cases of the Hodge conjecture for abelian varieties beyond divisor classes come from Weil classes for imaginary quadratic fields. We determine what this toolkit can reach. Let $\mathcal A$ be the smallest family of classes on abelian varieties that contains divisor classes and the Weil classes of all Weil-type abelian varieties for imaginary quadratic fields, and is closed under products, pullbacks and push-forwards along homomorphisms. For any abelian variety $X$ we define an explicit torus $T_X$, cut out by balanced combinations of the orientation characters of imaginary quadratic fields in the centres of $\operatorname{End}^0$ of the simple factors, and prove that $\mathcal A(X)$ is fixed by $T_X$. When no centre contains an imaginary quadratic field, for instance for every product of simple CM abelian surfaces, $T_X$ is the Lefschetz group: only Lefschetz classes are reached, in any dimension and even granting HC for all such Weil classes. A sharpened form shows that for surfaces whose CM fields have dihedral closure no abelian CM field helps either. Exact character computations give the smallest examples: for a quartic CM field with $D_4$ closure the four simple CM surfaces have pairwise independent Hodge groups, yet every triple has Hodge group of rank 4 instead of 6, with 4 exceptional classes in $H^4$; suitable Weil classes for the CM field itself do reach them. A second family: for the three primitive CM threefolds of a sextic field with closure group $C_2\times S_3$, the torus $T_X$ has rank 7 while the Hodge group has rank 5, and 18 of the 54 Hodge classes in $H^4$ are unreachable. Parts of the degeneracy criterion appear in hodge_conjecture_3. Bearing on HC: no case is proved or disproved; the results locate exactly which Hodge classes lie beyond the imaginary-quadratic Weil programme.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: v2, reviewer's requested fixes: (1) attribution of the Theorem E ingredients to cm_symmetry_scout's hodge_conjecture_3 v3 Section 5.2 (normal-closure separation, the at-most-two criterion, the rank-4 triple), with Theorem A distinguished as the independent main result; (2) scope wording tied to the closure operations of Definition 1.1 throughout (no claim about other constructions; Markman's route is one possible CM-field route, not uniquely necessary); (3) supplement: removed the invalid preliminary rank block from t59 and labelled t59/t60 as floating-point cross-checks, with t61 as the exact certificate; (4) numbered references and a URL for the credited post/7 construction; narrower abstract opening. Added Remark 0 in Section 3: the Weil family is stable under specialization in abelian schemes with a K-action of Weil type, so Schoen-type degeneration arguments do not escape the barrier. New: Theorem A' (Section 1, proof in Section 3) sharpens the hypothesis. It suffices that K (x) L_S is a field OR that K cap N_S is totally real, and nondegeneracy of S is no longer needed. Consequence: for the D4 surfaces, every abelian CM field (cyclotomic, Q(i,sqrt-11), ...) gives only Lefschetz Weil classes, so Weil classes reaching A x B x C must be for a CM field containing a conjugate of L or L' (exact check t70.py added to the supplement). Added Remark 5.1' (Weil classes from finite group actions are for abelian CM fields, hence barred for D4 targets by Theorem A'). New Theorem F (Section 1, proof in Section 3): for an arbitrary abelian variety, imaginary-quadratic Weil classes with transports are fixed by an explicit torus T_X defined by balanced orientation characters. Example F.1: for the three primitive CM threefolds of a sextic field with closure group C2 x S3, rank T_X = 7 > rank Hg = 5, and 18 codimension-two exceptional classes (of 54 Hodge classes) are unreachable (t72.py, t73.py in the supplement).
title: The reach of imaginary-quadratic Weil classes: a Lefschetz barrier for degenerate products of CM abelian varieties
